title: The Gifting Index
sub: Which perfume houses do people buy as gifts? A live site that answers from Google searches, drawn as six stems in one vase.
description: The Gifting Index: a live site by Riya Dutta comparing December demand for six perfume houses, Jo Malone London, Diptyque and Molton Brown against Le Labo, Byredo and Frédéric Malle, from Google Trends data refreshed daily, with a gift finder and a pressed-flower card.
facts: A live site comparing three classic gift names (Jo Malone London, Diptyque, Molton Brown) with three cult niche houses (Le Labo, Byredo, Frédéric Malle)
Google Trends searches, fetched every morning and saved with the site, with Wikipedia pageviews as a cross-check
The question, the analysis, the writing, the design and the build
HTML, CSS and JavaScript; Python and a GitHub Action for the daily data

sections.title: Guess which stem grows tallest.
sections.note: Tap the flower you think the next gifting moment makes biggest, then try the months. Scroll inside to find a perfume for someone, or open the live site full screen.

items.t: Some perfume names everyone recognises; others have an insider following. When people shop for someone else, does that difference show?
No sales data from any brand. Only what’s public, and the answer had to keep itself up to date.

sections.title: The names people recognise jump every December.
sections.lead: Searches for Jo Malone, Diptyque and Molton Brown roughly double each December. Le Labo, Byredo and Frédéric Malle rise by about half.

sections.note: Google searches in December against each year’s typical month, worldwide, every full year since 2016 (the niche houses from when Google has enough searches for them). The gift names were taller in all eight Decembers with data for both groups, 2018 to 2025. Figures as of November 2026; the live site recalculates them every day.

sections.title: Checks that changed the story.
sections.intro: Each of these made the site claim less than a first pass would have.

items.d: I tested nine more houses before adding two. Penhaligon’s and Acqua di Parma behave like the niche houses, so “classic” here means the name people reach for as a present, not the oldest.
An early pass found a March bump for Jo Malone that looked like Mother’s Day in the UK. Medians showed it was a few one-off spikes, so it was cut.
A September spike for Jo Malone seemed to leave a +67% lasting lift. With the normal run-up to Christmas removed, it was +16%.

items.t: Let the data write the headline
items.d: The figures and the year count are calculated from the current data. If a niche house out-gifts the classics one year, the page says so.

sections.title: Made to be used, not only read.

tiles.d: Guess which stem the next gifting moment grows tallest. The buds open into each house’s flower, and the months show how the year moves.
Pick who it’s for, the occasion and up to three things they love. It suggests one of 30 scents from the six houses, leaning to the gift names for others and the niche houses for yourself.
Press a month flower for someone and spray it with a scent; its notes are pressed beside the flower. Download or share it. Nothing typed is saved or sent.

paras: This December is the first live season for the new site. The page will show, as it happens, whether the gift names hold their lead for a ninth year.
